name: Verify a Google Sheets lead list (Email Verifier)

parameters.content:
# Verify a Google Sheets lead list

Reads rows that have no `status` yet, verifies them in batches, writes the verdict back next to each address. Re-running only picks up new rows, so it is safe on a schedule.

## Your sheet needs these columns

`email` · `status` · `sub_status` · `score` · `catch_all` · `disposable` · `verified_at`

Only `email` needs values. The rest are filled in.

## Setup (once)

**1. Get an Apify token** — https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations

**2. Create the n8n credential**
Credentials → New → **Header Auth**
- Name: `Apify API`
- Header name: `Authorization`
- Header value: `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN`

Every HTTP node here already points at that credential by name. No token is stored in this file.

**3. Connect Google Sheets** on the two Sheets nodes and pick your document and sheet.

## Cost

Pay-per-event: one charge per address that gets a verdict, including undeliverable and unknown — the work was done either way. From $0.55 per 1,000, tiered by your Apify plan.

Current pricing: https://apify.com/sumitr_mardy/email-verifier/pricing

Actor: https://apify.com/sumitr_mardy/email-verifier
Templates & docs: https://github.com/sumitrmardy/email-verifier-api

## Why results are matched by address, not by row order

The Actor groups addresses by domain to reuse connections, so results come back in a different order than they went in. Matching by position would silently put the wrong verdict on the wrong person.

This workflow builds a lookup keyed on `email` and `normalized_email` — `normalized_email` is there because a Gmail address written `J.Doe+news@gmail.com` comes back as `jdoe@gmail.com`.
